thread.title: Today Is Apple's Most Important Earnings Announcement in Years

title: Today Is Apple's Most Important Earnings Announcement in Years
text:

https://www.barrons.com/articles/apple-earnings-stock-51548727039 Today Could Be Apple’s Most Important Earnings Announcement in Years By Jan. 29, 2019 5:30 a.m. ET Order Reprints Anthony Quintano Text size
Apple is no stranger to high-stakes announcements, but they’re usually of the product variety—a new phone, tablet, or watch, say. Tuesday’s earnings report , however, could actually rival an Apple keynote for attention and importance. I’d go so far as to call it Apple’s most important earnings announcement in years.
Apple opened a can of worms during its last earnings call , on Nov. 1, when the company said it would no longer provide “unit sales” data for the iPhone, iPad, or Mac. Wall Street analysts have relied on that data for years to model Apple’s profits. By making the change—just as the iPhone was struggling —Apple gave the impression that sales were even worse than many thought. And it caused Wall Street to scramble for new ways to understand the company.
So analysts will be looking for some help tomorrow, as Apple CEO Tim Cook fields questions on the company’s quarterly conference call. Surely, Cook and his PR folks have spent a good deal of time practicing those answers.
In justifying the decision last quarter to pull back on unit sales, CFO Luca Maestri told investors that “a unit of sale is less relevant today than it was in the past.” The company promised to provide gross margin information on its faster-growing services business, the segment that includes iCloud, iTunes, and Apple Music. That wasn’t enough to stem the worries about units, though. The fear was compounded when Apple warned about its December quarter results in early January. Apple stock (AAPL) is down 30% since the Nov. 1 earnings call.
Apple may not talk about its stock price tomorrow, but the selloff will weigh heavily on the mood of the call.
I wouldn’t be surprised if the company offers up other new kinds of data, perhaps a way of tracking recurring revenue inside its services segment. We don’t really know how much repeatable subscription revenue Apple gets from iCloud and Apple Music. That’s the kind of stuff investors value at a premium. And it could be one way for Apple to finally change the subject away from disappointing iPhone sales.
